Lance (YC W26) has raised $5 million in seed funding to build AI agents that run hotel operations. The round was backed by Y Combinator and SV Angel, alongside operators, founders, and funds connected to OpenAI, Expedia, and the Johnson Family / OTO Development. The San Francisco company is targeting a stubbornly manual part of hospitality: calls, guest requests, sales inquiries, scheduling, maintenance, housekeeping, and manager reporting still moving through phone trees, shared inboxes, radios, spreadsheets, and legacy hotel systems. Lance's bet is that hotels do not need another narrow chatbot. They need an agent layer that can answer, understand, route, and execute operational work across the property. That makes this less of a front-desk automation story and more of an operating-system wedge. Lance Live handles voice calls in under a second, the sales email agent turns group inquiries into human-approved replies, and the operations layer produces schedules, work orders, and daily manager reports. The company says its systems are already deployed in real hotels handling real guests. The sharper question is whether hotels will buy AI agents as labor relief, revenue capture, or infrastructure. Lance is trying to make the answer all three. Quick facts👇 ● founders: Caleb Chan ; Gavin Brennen ; Gatik Trivedi ● total capital raised: $5 million ● HQ: San Francisco, California ● Investors: Y Combinator ; SV Angel ; operators, founders, and funds connected to OpenAI, Expedia, and the Johnson Family / OTO Development The interesting part is that Lance is not pitching AI as a layer above hotel operations. It is pitching AI as the workforce interface for the property itself. ...more ...more

This was my calendar the day after YC Launch. I’ve heard founders describe product market fit as a pull. Not you trying to convince people, but people showing up because something resonates. These past few weeks felt like that. My calendar filled with general managers, ownership groups, asset managers. Different brands, different markets. Many of them reached out on their own. What stuck with me wasn’t hype. It was how familiar the conversations sounded. We would ask about their operations and within a few minutes the same themes would surface. Phones ringing with no one free to answer. Sales inquiries sitting in inboxes longer than they should, some never followed up. Managers stepping into line-level tasks just to keep the day moving. Millions of dollars in lost revenue No one called it a crisis. It was more like a constant background weight that everyone had quietly accepted as normal. That’s what made it feel like something real. We’re building Lance (YC W26) around that reality. If you’re in hospitality and this sounds familiar, that’s probably why. ...more ...more

activity.title: This guy knows hotels.

Company culture isn’t a buzzword to me… it’s the whole game. Those who know me know I’m borderline obsessed with it, because culture is what separates “just another company” from a team that actually wins. It’s the heartbeat, the energy, the way people show up for each other and for their customers. Plenty of companies talk about culture, put it on slide decks and careers pages, but very few actually live it, consistently, in the everyday moments when it really counts. The founders of Lance don’t just say they care about culture – you feel it. Ownership, curiosity, and genuine care for their team and the hospitality world are baked into how the team operates, which is exactly why I love working with them. Advising the founders, collaborating with the team, and helping build a first-class product for hospitality has been a blast. And the best part? We’re just getting started. Stay tuned. Excited to share I joined Lance as a Founding Engineer! Before this, I'd never set foot in a hotel back office. Sitting down with housekeepers, maintenance techs, and front desk agents changed how I think about this whole industry. The amount of coordination it takes to keep a property running is staggering, and so much of it still happens through workarounds for tools that were never built for the people using them. We're fixing that, making the day-to-day communication and operations across a property something that just works. Thank you to Shreyas Diwan and my team at Salesforce for the last few years, and to the Lance founders for the opportunity. Super grateful to be part of such a talented and welcoming team, and excited for everything we're going to build.

Super excited to be shaping the future of hospitality as a Founding Product Manager at Lance ! It's been the best first month of late night builds and running from hotel to hotel (shoutout battle bus) with the greatest team. That understanding doesn't come from us, it comes from every housekeeper, maintenance worker (product drop incoming 👀), front desk agent, and more who have spent hours walking us through their days and letting us ask too many questions. You all are the reason we do any of this. So excited to be part of this incredible family and for everything to come! I'm also actively hiring an AI Engineer for my team, so reach out if interested :)

Software as a Service? We're aiming higher. We're building Software as a Solution. Three weeks ago, I didn't know what a pull request was. Today I'm shipping them, and watching them get used by real hotels. Here's some context. I'm not an engineer by background. I'm a hospitality person. Front desks, late night check ins, solving problems for the person standing right in front of me. I come from the industry of people and relationships. In three weeks at Lance (YC W26) , I've learned more than I imagined possible, about design, shipping product, coding, and what it actually takes to find real solutions. And I owe a lot of that to the incredible engineers and tech minds I get to work alongside, people who have led me, shown me the ropes, and helped me grow in ways I never expected. I've shipped my first features. I've watched code I wrote land in the hands of real hotel teams. And I've had customers tell me directly how much they value something that didn't exist before I built it. That's a feeling I won't forget. Because I've been the front desk agent slammed at 11pm. I know and feel that job in my bones. So every feature I build has one goal: make their lives easier. We're not building features for the sake of features. We're building solutions for the people I used to stand beside. We're building something special here at Lance. If helping real people find real solutions sounds interesting to you, come build with us.
